thread.title: ams AG's Business Wins Offset Some Of The Near-Term Apple Turbulence - AMS AG ADR (OTCMKTS:AMSSY)

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: ams AG's Business Wins Offset Some Of The Near-Term Apple Turbulence - AMS AG ADR (OTCMKTS:AMSSY)
text:
Growth semiconductor stories aren’t where you go if you can’t handle some drama and volatility, and ams ( OTCPK:AMSSY )(AMS.S) has certainly provided that. Although the shares have basically matched the SOX since my last write-up in mid-January (and outperformed Finisar ( FNSR ) and Himax ( HIMX )), it hasn’t been a smooth ride as investors have had to digest some encouraging wins as well as a big cut to guidance on reduced expectations for Apple ’s ( AAPL ) high-end phone production.
I continue to believe that ams is a good way to play the growth of 3D sensing, not just in consumer devices, but also in auto and industrial applications. There will be no shortage of competition, and ams’s relationship will likely add volatility (and likely some margin challenges), but I think the long-term potential is worth it.
Some Fits And Starts As a company that is still on the front-end of its opportunity, I’m not all that surprised that there has been some “turbulence” to ams’s performance, but it does underline some of the risks. Fourth quarter results were strong in some respects (revenue up 250% yoy with significant operating margin expansion), and likewise there were some good things in the first quarter results (revenue up 147% yoy and double-digit operating margins).
Of course I’m leading to a “but”, and that is the company’s sharp revision to second quarter guidance. The weaker than expected demand for Apple’s iPhone X has led to a much faster than expected product transition cycle and channel inventory run-down, leading ams to a revenue target for the second quarter a third lower than expected. With that ams is going to be seeing much worse factory utilization and that’s going to hit margins hard. Management was bullish about the prospects for a second half ramp from Apple, but delays in finalizing specifications will keep ams from manufacturing in anticipation of that transition.
New Wins Are Encouraging, But Also Necessary Apple is likely to be a major component of ams’s revenue for some time to come, but ams has to win business outside of Apple for this investment thesis to work. Fortunately there have been some wins since my last update that give me some encouragement on that process.
ams has announced its first major 3D order with an Asian phone OEM, where it will supply both the WLO and VCSEL. This deal should start shipping at the end of 2018, and while management didn’t identify the company, what they did say about the customer leads me to think it is either Samsung or Huawei (a company with its own app processor). Either would be significant and a win with Samsung would help balance some of the seasonality of Apple’s business. The company also won a sizable order from a phone OEM for a power component; this deal should be worth “several hundred million dollars” starting in 2019.
The company also announced a significant 3D LiDAR order. Although it won’t start shipping until 2021, the order has already been nearly doubled from a lifetime value of $600 million to $1.1 billion.
Those are good wins, but ams has to build from here. I believe that 3D sensing will become a fixture on high-end phones, but it is going to take time. Likewise, depth sensing on the back of phones could be an important incremental opportunity, but probably not for a couple of years (at least). I’m also looking for ams to win some business in the coming years from industrial automation and robotics companies, as I believe the company’s 3D sensors are enabling technology for more sophisticated machine vision and factory automation technologies (including mobile robots).
The Opportunity Between Apple and other customer wins, I expect ams to see significant revenue acceleration over the next three years, from around CHF 1.5B in 2018 (ams is switching over to U.S. dollar reporting) to 2B in 2019 and close to 2.5B in 2020. I expect this acceleration to facilitate a meaningful expansion of margins, with non-GAAP operating margin reaching the high 20%’s (and maybe close to 30%) in 2020. Longer term, I see significant ongoing opportunities in optical, imagining, environmental, and audio sensing that can support double-digit revenue growth through 2022. I’d also expect ams to stay involved in wireless power and wireless connectivity, as they are enabling technologies for the sensing, VCSEL, and LiDAR businesses.
If ams can reach CHF 2B in revenue in 2019, 3B in 2022, and 4B-plus in 2026 and drive adjusted FCF margins in the low-to-mid 20%’s (which I believe it can), the shares offer double-digit potential on a DCF basis. I also like to use an operating margin-driven EV/revenue approach to value semiconductor stocks. By this approach ams shares look about 15% undervalued today, with upside if revenue and margins outperform (but vice versa if they underperform).
The Bottom Line I expect no shortage of competition for ams, whether its smaller companies like Himax or large companies like STM ( STM ), Sony ( SNE ), and Infineon ( OTCQX:IFNNY ). Although I believe ams has the product/technology attributes to be a market leader, that is by no means proven. And even if ams does develop into a market leader, there will be plenty of ups and downs along the way. I like the opportunity at today’s valuation, but this certainly is not an investment for those who can’t stomach above-average volatility.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
